body:
Closes #458

Adds native ML-DSA-65 and SHAKE, then composes ML-DSA-65 and Ed25519 under the exact JOSE/COSE draft-04 and LAMPS draft-19 construction. One detached COSE Sign1 carries both signatures; verification requires both components, the declared protected algorithm and the original protected bytes. Strict parsing rejects ambiguous headers, unsupported critical instructions, malformed component encodings, attached payloads and trailing data. Existing Ed25519 byte goldens remain unchanged.

The production Writer requires an explicit randomness provider for composite signatures. Provider failure refuses the operation atomically. Caller-supplied typed composite keys and resolution, eager and evented signature observation, file keyring verification, RDF policy verification, compaction and certification all use the same implementation. Compaction and certification require a packaging signer; they retain detached authorship signatures with the correct current root/index binding and classify packaging separately. GTS reuses the existing workspace SHA-512 package through its sha2 runtime edge; no new external dependency package, duplicate crypto implementation or semantic Cargo feature was added.

Qualification found and fixed a timestamp boundary that could mistake authored content for packaging. Both the producer and conservative provenance classifier now use the existing XSD dateTime parser and require an explicit UTC timezone. Malformed or non-UTC source facts retain authored content and exact COSE; invalid producer parameters refuse before signing. Valid Z, +00:00, -00:00, extended/negative years and legal 24:00:00 remain accepted with caller bytes preserved.

Validation: the required `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 make check` passed on its captured pre-correction source, covering 21,045 native tests, 460 doc tests, all normal policy/generator gates, the preserve-order consumer, core ring fences and actual release wasm compilation of 31 publishable libraries plus bench. The existing default ignores are accounted for. That gate is reused only for unaffected input closures, not relabeled as execution on corrected source. Current correction checks passed all 1,361 GTS/RDF native cases and 13 docs, all 11 public compaction/certification groups in actual Node/wasm, workspace all-target clippy with warnings denied, strict affected docs, hygiene/dependency/generator checks and unchanged independent producer/consumer probe replays. Current `make wasm` also actually rebuilt the required 31 publishable libraries plus bench under the normal release profile. The final 52-path source manifest is SHA256 `e899501200bd56af128b504c84c9ca1c8681f6c92fe3719815bb6fa635c6567d`.

Independent evidence includes all 70 official NIST ML-DSA records and the complete pinned IETF composite answer. Actual Node/wasm runner evidence covers the primitive, COSE, Writer and compaction/certification entry points; unchanged input closures are explicitly recorded instead of representing those executions as new runs. Hosted CI is not represented as completed by local qualification.

The current official IANA allocation still leaves -58 unassigned; -49 is standalone ML-DSA-65 and is not substituted. The governed GTS upstream at `0d1c8299c9411ea4ead853e31721d42ea66f081e` has only its two EdDSA COSE vectors and no published composite vector. Primary known answers therefore do not establish shared-engine GTS composite interoperability. Construction pins and these limits are documented; no governed vector was changed.

Callers must provide dedicated independent component keys and fresh cryptographic randomness. Functional known answers do not prove compiler/JIT/hardware timing behavior or formal FIPS certification. Owned secret clearing does not guarantee removal of compiler copies, registers or spills. The separately posted confidence answers describe these boundaries.

The attached approved plan preserves its original planning snapshot and historical progress footer. Signed task checkpoints and final qualification record current implementation and validation; publication and hosted acceptance are verified separately.
